name: Varbase Components
description: Components-handler module for the Varbase distribution: a theme/component switcher and self-heal layer for the Drupal Canvas (cva) SDC stack. It migrates all component references (config, content, Canvas page regions, text-field paths) when the default theme changes, heals stale SDC component version hashes after rebuild/module/theme installs, hides administrative Canvas components, exposes an active_theme Twig variable, and adds Views style + exposed-form plugins that render a view through an SDC.
project_description:
Varbase Components is the components-handler module of the Varbase distribution. In the 4.0.x line it was rebuilt around Drupal Canvas (the `cva` project's `canvas` module) instead of the earlier UI Patterns / UI Icons recipe stack: its only hard dependencies are `drupal/cva` (~1) and core `views`, and it ships no Single Directory Components, Twig templates or component libraries of its own. It is the glue and maintenance layer that keeps a Canvas SDC-based site consistent.

Its central piece is ActiveThemeChangeSubscriber, which listens on the config SAVE event. When `system.theme:default` changes AND both the old and new themes declare `auto_switch_components: true` in their `.info.yml`, it performs a full re-theming migration: a regex rewrite of the old theme's machine name (and its `themes/(contrib|custom)/<theme>/` filesystem paths and `sdc.<theme>.` component IDs) across all active config; a rewrite of `dependencies.theme` lists; a clone of Canvas `page_region` config entities to the new theme; a rewrite of the `component_id` column in every `component_tree` content field table; a replace of old theme filesystem paths in text/body fields; and a heal of stale component_version hashes in both config and content so the new theme's active SDC versions are used. All database writes go through Drupal's query builder with placeholders and REPLACE() expressions.

A second concern is component-version healing. Canvas regenerates its SDC component config entities (with new version hashes) on cache rebuild, module install and theme install. VarbaseComponentsHooks weights the module heavier than Canvas and runs `heal()` from the `rebuild`, `modules_installed` and `themes_installed` hooks so any config or content still pinning an old version hash is rewritten to the active version, silencing Canvas's "Component version not found, falling back to active version" warning. The same repair is exposed as the Drush command `varbase-components:fix-versions`.

Third, it curates the Canvas component library: a `component_presave` hook creates the components listed in `varbase_components.settings:hidden_canvas_components` disabled (admin/duplicate blocks and SDCs such as project-browser, AI dashboard, and the Webshare share block/component), `hook_install()` disables any that already exist, and `themes_uninstalled` deletes orphaned `sdc.<theme>.*` Canvas component configs left behind by an uninstalled theme. A `#[Hook('preprocess')]` still exposes the default theme machine name as the `active_theme` Twig variable, and a `varbase_components/aos` library wires the Animate-On-Scroll (AOS) vendor library, attached when a component selects an animation.

Finally it adds two Views plugins that render a view through an SDC: a `components_views_style` style plugin (places rendered rows into a chosen component slot and maps static prop values) and a `components_exposed_form` exposed-form plugin (renders the exposed filter form inside a component's `filters` slot). Both list only components that declare `use_in_views: true`. Three Drush commands (`varbase-components:switch-theme`, `:fix-versions`, `:scan-refs`) expose the migration/heal/audit logic for manual runs. The `~11.4.0` core pin ties the site's core updates to the Varbase release cycle. Sponsored and developed by Vardot.
